newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: RESEARCH ALERT-S.Korean semicon profits seen down.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-S.Korean semicon profits seen down.

text.p: Dongwon Economic Research Institute said on Monday that South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co Ltd and LG Semicon Co Ltd are expected to post net profits in 1996 considerably lower than seen a year ago.

Samsung was seen posting a net profit of 405 billion won this year, narrowing from 2.5 trillion last year, while LG Semicon net profit was seen shrinking to 104 billion won in 1996 from 779 billion a year ago.

The institute, which is a reseach arm of Dongwon Securities, also said in a statement that unlisted Hyundai Electric Industrial Co Ltd's net profit was forecast down to 74 billion won from 835 billion.
It blamed the falling profits on a global oversupply of dynamic random access memory chips (DRAM).
"Oversupply of DRAM in the world market is expected to continue until the third quarter of 1997, but supply and demand is likely to balance out in the last quarter of 1997," the statement said.
It said the semiconductor industry was seen improving in 1998 in line with slowing facility investment.

"Net profits of the three companies are unlikely to see any significant recovery in 1997 because of the burden from depreciation and financial costs resulting from continued facility investments," Dongwon said.
"However, the profits are expected to improve in 1998 along with a semiconductor market recovery," it said.
Samsung Electronics's turnover is seen at 17 trillion won this year, slightly higher than 16 trillion a year ago, the institute said.
It sees LG Semicon posting sales of 2.4 trillion this year against 2.5 trillion last year and Hyundai Electronics of 3.6 trillion won in 1996 versus 3.9 trillion in 1995.
